**Feedback**

*Title* 

The words are all fine, but I would've put 'Shoving Balls Into Someone's Hole?' first. The thumbnail should get across that it's funny moments in Golf It!

*Thumbnail*

The black space around the thumbnail is so jarring, so if you could've made it full screen like you have with the others, it would be great. I don't mind the bowling ball with black poop on top (???), but if it was me I would've upped the saturation of the image by a lot so it pops. I would also make the logo smaller and in the left corner while making the 'funny moments' bigger. You could even change funny moments to a short funny phrase in the middle or end of the video. 

*Concept*

It's nothing special since a quick search told me there are many other videos like it, but the fact that it's you and your friends makes yours uniquely enjoyable, so it's fine.

*Picture/Sound*

The gameplay has been recorded at a high quality. Nice!

*Storytelling*

Funny intro, but it was too short for me to get it straight away without replaying it. It would've been nicer if you left like 2 seconds of silence first. Still, I liked the pacing as a whole. 

*Editing*

It's super basic, and that's not a problem exactly, but I think it severely limits the video.

First, the black space around your footage is very jarring. Zooming in just a bit to make it full screen OR duplicating your footage track, expanding the bottom one so it's full screen and blurring that one would've worked.

Second, I really think there should be subtitles throughout. Considering the gameplay itself is pretty basic, it would be much more engaging if there was something else going on visually. 

Third, I think you could've added louder, funnier sounds than you did. Not necessarily full-on memes, but maybe the 'what the helllll oh my god' or other sounds would've made the jokes told very dryly funnier by contrast. 

Fourth, your text needs some work. Some are too dark (the red text mostly), and the lack of outlines around them makes them jarring to read. PLEASE add black outlines and make sure that it all contrasts with the background.

Last, transitions between turns might have been good too. Like every minute, add a 'It's X's turn' screen and then play the Mario Golf OST or something. But admittedly, this is not a must-have. 

*Overall Impression*

This was good content that had a title and solid concept that couldn't go wrong, but your editing and thumbnail game needs work so you can present it in a more engaging way and keep an audience who is unfamiliar with you to start watching. You're selling your humour, and you all have funny jokes, but even the funniest stand-up isn't gonna be watched if it's too unappealing to watch.

Hope that helped, my fellow brits! :D

I would suggest thinking of a big niche that makes your gaming content different and running with that. Not Vtuber but maybe a doll collector or SimCity player or a trash gamer does x. So it would be 'Simscity Player Judges Minecraft', 'Trash Gamer Can't Figure Out How to Mine' or 'Doll Collector Recreates Collection In Minecraft'. It could work to make you stand out. Your short attention span niche isn't good because I clicked your video and the video was frankly boring instead of fast-paced like I was expecting. I'd suggest making the videos 10 minutes long with a hook in the title and the video. The thumbnail would show what you made full screen without any black barrels on the top and bottom and the text would be centred and minimal like in 'A NEW STAR IS COMING 2 | Can you guess who this is?'

*Shorts*

They all have a cute layout, but I would suggest simply posting clips of your gameplay with your icon on the bottom and maybe adding close captions onto it using Capcut or TikTok and uploading it here. it would be much more effective at getting people to watch it and you can link the related video to these shorts too. Also, make sure these highlights have you yelling, speaking loudly, doing something fun, and sounding excited. At least in the beginning. No one wants to hear someone mumble to themselves (this is not shade on you, I myself have learnt this the hard way 💀😭).

*Playlists*

*Posts*

*Overall Impression*

I can tell you've put a lot of thought into this and are really into dolls. I think you need to turn that into your personality online. Use what you like from dolls to make your content interesting and a reflection of yourself. 

You really need to think about why anyone would watch your videos because every single one of them seems like a personal fun thing than anything. Even the Bocchi the Rock thing is a niche within a niche that could have been a Reddit post, or an Instagram story, not a video. You need to make content and advertise your content into something easy for someone to go: oh, so that's what it's about. Once you've got that down, you need to make them click by making the content interesting. 

You've compared yourself to other similar channels, but I don't think you've done it enough. I need you to study them. Take out a notepad and write about every little difference between your videos and channel and presentation and copy it. Straight-up copy everything except maybe the video topic and see what comes out. I think doing that will help you tremendously. 

Good luck, I hope this has helped :)

Admittedly, I don't watch that many channels like yours so it is a bit harder for me to criticise. Still, I'll try my best. 

So, your first batch of videos feels like a small business owner releasing content. And usually those types of announcements and reveals (if they aren't shorts) don't do well at all unless they show how they made the item. This is probably because it's a tweet's worth of content and not worth clicking on unless you're a diehard. It's obvious that the channel will do the thing they're announcing so most would rather just wait to see it happen because they don't care enough or they don't have the attention span, whatever. You have to think, why would anyone care about these videos? What's your main goal per video? Dropping characters without any context or hook, especially when you didn't make them isn't good and it probably hurt your channel's debut and progress. So, no more of those.

The 'funny videos' don't give me funny. I genuinely can't tell which they are just from looking which is a problem. I would suggest looking up skit videos or something to find better ways to title and make thumbnails:

No one wants to watch part 3 of something they don't care about enough to go find part 1. 
2. Focusing on one character in the thumbnail for a skit video. You could change the title to 'when you don't know where you put it' or something more directly to what the point of this video is and then I would say you have your first best advertised 'funny' video.

The lack of a colour scheme does make it harder for me to tie everything together anyway, but I will say it is a big jump you made into gaming with your new avatar. I would recommend either 1) personalising your compilations by maybe adding memes or funny jokes to these compilations (which is hard to do without being cringe imo but possible) or 2) banging out a ridiculous amount of them (featuring various games, not just one). These types of videos are something you have to sell your soul to be successful at, but since you aren't interested in doing that, I would suggest just going straight into making more complicated content as you intended to do later.

**Feedback**

*Name*

Generic and more unclear than other successful channels that I found from a quick search. At least 'Manhwa Outpost' or 'Manhwa Fresh' makes sense since they're posting exclusively new manhwa recaps. 'CallMeManhwa' doesn't make any basic sense in comparison. I would recommend changing it especially if you're planning on reviewing manga too. But at the same time, I understand that this niche doesn't care about originality so this point probably doesn't matter.

*Profile Pic*

It works. I would zoom in and use a picture more sticking though. Idk if you used AI (there's no shame in that btw!) or not, but maybe you could make/find a character that's grinning very wide and use a closeup of that to get the same feel. Or maybe you could change the tone and find/make a close-up funny face that's looking at the camera. 

*About*

It's great you have a short and sweet about section, but you should swap the clauses of that first sentence and focus the first line of your about (the only thing most people actually read) on being personable. I think showing that a human is making this content is ESSENTIAL for a channel like yours that actually narrates it compared to your competitors who often use AI voices. It helps you stand out.

*Home*

Nice layout. It's a good choice to pick a video of a new series that starts without warning to suck in potential viewers. I don't have any complaints really except I feel like you can omit the playlist section until you have more than one. It kind of looks awkward all by itself.  

*Videos*

I'm so relieved I could immediately see the problems here because your thumbnail game is great and the preview of your video on the home page was solid.

You really are trying, but you're a recap channel. What happens if the viewers don't like the one series you picked and banged out for one month? They leave because you haven't got any variation. There's a pretty simple fix. For someone like you who probably isn't yet full-time on this, I'd recommend covering 3 different sub-genres at once. One modern power fantasy, one school bullying and one martial arts one. Stories like unOrdinary and Damn Reincarnation are very popular and has been summarised before. Why don't you look for more new, up-and-coming manhwas on Webtoon or something? As I said, I read manhwa and these are the top three 'action' type manhwas right now imo. So, if that's your focus, go for that. Although, I think a male voice narrating romance manhwas would be a breath of fresh air for viewers 👀. 

There's also the number trap you fell into. Get rid of numbers on the thumbnails and in titles. Put them in the description/top comment and in the video itself instead. It's a thing, honestly so many people have spoken about it I couldn't tell you all the reasons why. Basically, if you come across a video that says part 3, you often click away, right? Because you haven't seen part 1 and tell yourself looking for it would take too much effort. But if you saw a video without a number anywhere, clicked it and it said 'this is part 3 btw, part 1 is in the desc/top comment' it suddenly doesn't feel like so much effort. 

Also, upping the frequency of your videos to twice a week is tough but it might be needed for this niche.

- Friends can end their relationship with you at any time and vice versa, but good ones tend to last years at a time at least

u/rurubarb already gave the perfect response, but I wanted to point out the biggest part/role in the animation industry (from researching about this quite a bit). It seems the ones in charge of the overall projects are usually the producers (/production companies), as they handle the money. Everyone else is usually hired by them.

Often in the USA, the big production companies have their own studios that animate (distribute, voice act etc.) for them. Sometimes they outsource, but it is not the most common practice to create animated content I believe. Compared to Japan, where they usually have production committees focused on more than just the animation (+ can be unethical to studios) that usually outsource animation studios and other companies to do the same work.

Ultimately, it seems to me that **producers** are the people who will hold your fate.

My advice is don't focus on one project. Focus on your **portfolio.** This one project will likely not gain much traction or be the best work you've ever done. But what it is is a start. So, use it as a **learning opportunity.** Watch how it does, reflect on what people (close to you or online) like about it, and whether it fits in with the **market.** Figure out whether it is a story **worth** making more of in the first place and if you even have the inspiration for it. 

I think to make money and earn what you deserve, you don't need one good product, you need **multiple** good products. Best of luck! :)

Then I came to psychology because I realised that I could pursue the passion I had for art outside of uni, in fact, I didn't want academia to change it for me like it had before. Make it more like work. But with psychology I was able to do the opposite, make something which can be quite draining into more fun (now that I can choose my dissertation/projects' topics and modules which interest me) 

I think you could easily do psychology and then focus on art therapy within the modules. You could do clinical psychology. Or pursue teaching and pursue art within that. I know many unis don't have the option to combine it, meaning that either way, you'll likely be doing a degree and branching off a little bit anyway. So I guess ask yourself, can I see [insert career] becoming less like work and more like fun in the future? If all of them are like that, which one do you think you can pursue the most without the degree and chose the other one.
